title: Affine uniform truncation maps for a derived coproduct
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $I$ be a set and $E_i$ a family in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $S\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with maps $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ which exhibit an ambient coproduct. Write $F_q=H^q\circ Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For every integer $q$ and affine open $U\subseteq Y$, there is an integer $a$ such that both maps $\Gamma(U,\bigoplus_i F_q(E_i))\to\Gamma(U,\bigoplus_i F_q(\tau_{\ge a}E_i))$ and $\Gamma(U,F_q(S))\to\Gamma(U,F_q(\tau_{\ge a}S))$ induced by the canonical projections $\pi_a:T\to\tau_{\ge a}T$ are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_Y(U)$-modules. The first map is sections of the coproduct of the maps $F_q(\pi_a(E_i))$, rather than a claimed coproduct formula for sections.

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums] to identify the cohomology of the given ambient coproduct with the direct sum of the quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves of its summands. Express this sum as the directed colimit of finite sums: [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] give quasi-coherence, including the empty sum.

Restrict f to U; its target is affine and quasi-compact and it remains qcqs. Exact restriction preserves sums, quasi-coherent cohomology and canonical truncations. Restricted K-injective representatives compute the restricted derived direct image, naturally in all objects and in the truncation projections.

Apply the uniform upper-bound clause of 08D5(2) to the restricted morphism. Choose a single sufficiently negative a (for instance a <= q-N, with N its upper bound) so that the direct images of tau_<a E_i and tau_<a S vanish in both degrees q and q+1. Shift compatibility and the uniform bound make this choice independent of i. The long exact sequence of the truncation triangle therefore makes every q-th truncation projection an isomorphism after restriction. The separate objectwise existence clause is insufficient for this familywise choice.

Restriction preserves coproducts, so the coproduct of these restricted isomorphisms is invertible, also for an empty family. Apply evaluation at the top open of U to this isomorphism and to the isomorphism for S. Under the natural restriction comparisons these are exactly the two module maps in the statement; no assertion that sections commute with coproducts is made.

lean.statement: theorem exists_derivedDirectImage_coproduct_affine_truncation {X Y : Scheme.{u₁}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))] (I : Type u₁) (E : I → schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (S : schemeDerivedCategory X) (ι : ∀ i, (E i).obj ⟶ S) (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk S ι)) (q : ℤ) (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : ∃ a : ℤ, IsIso ((SheafOfModules.evaluation (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) (op U)).map (Limits.Sigma.map (fun i ↦ (schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ a).app (E i).obj)))) ∧ IsIso ((SheafOfModules.evaluation (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) (op U)).map ((schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ a).app S)))
